newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen up slightly on Wed.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen up slightly on Wed.

text.p: Polish shares on Tuesday inched up after a four-session dip and analysts said the bourse's recent 38 percent bull run in which large-cap stocks surged had led to a flat market in which small-cap stocks thrived.

They said the main market should rise slightly again on Wednesday, fuelled by more large speculative rises by small-cap fundamentally less sound firms, and that a deeper profit-taking correction could soon hit.
"It looks like the end of the growth phase because...fundamentally weak firms are starting to strongly grow," said Ryszard Sikora of Bank Slaski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.2 percent to 18,122.0 points and turnover rose 17.8 percent to 195.3 million zlotys ($64.3 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 49 to 26 with 14 stocks flat.
None of the main market's eight top gainers on Tuesday make up more than 0.5 percent of the WIG index.
Bank Komunalny rose the daily maximum 10 percent and glass maker Irena 9.6 percent in moderate trade.

Construction firm Espebepe rose 9.5 percent and did not trade after price fixing due to excess demand, with some investors possibly speculating before the firm's creditors meet on March 14, analysts said.

Mass privatisation NFI units jumped 4.8 percent to 175 zlotys ($57.6) in 65.4-million-zloty ($21.5 million) trade in the bourse's regular session, buoyed by recent foreign analysts' appraisals of the units at $80 ($243) and higher, analysts said.
The units fell 0.6 percent to 176 zlotys ($57.9) in 77.1-million-zloty ($25.4 million) continuous trade, where most stocks rose and turnover was at 19.8 million zlotys ($6.5 million).
